segments.text: How many people visited the Great Exhibition of 1851?
segments.translation: 有多少人参观了1851年的世博会？

segments.text: Perhaps the most extraordinary building of the 19th century was the Crystal Palace
segments.translation: 也许19世纪最不寻常的建筑就是水晶宫，

segments.text: which was built in Hyde Park for the Great Exhibition of 1851.
segments.translation: 它建在海德公园，是为1851年的世博会而建造的。

segments.text: The Crystal Palace was different from all other buildings in the world, for it was made of iron and glass.
segments.translation: 水晶宫与世界上所有其他建筑都不同，因为它是用钢铁和玻璃造的。

segments.text: It was one of the biggest buildings of all time and a lot of people from many countries came to see it.
segments.translation: 它是有史以来最大的建筑之一，许多国家的人都来参观它。

segments.text: A great many goods were sent to the exhibition from various parts of the world.
segments.translation: 大量的商品从世界各地运来参展。

segments.text: There was also a great deal of machinery on display.
segments.translation: 还展出了许多机器设备。

segments.text: The most wonderful piece of machinery on show was Nasmyth's steam hammer.
segments.translation: 展出的最了不起的机器设备是内史密斯的蒸汽锤。

segments.text: Though in those days travelling was not as easy as it is today,
segments.translation: 虽然在那个年代旅行不像今天这样方便，

segments.text: steam boats carried thousands of visitors across the Channel from Europe.
segments.translation: 轮船还是把成千上万的游客从欧洲运过英吉利海峡。

segments.text: On arriving in England, they were, taken to the Crystal Palace by train.
segments.translation: 他们一到英国就乘火车前往水晶宫。

segments.text: There were six million visitors in all,
and the profits from the exhibition were used to build museums and colleges.
segments.translation: 博览会的收入被用来建造博物馆和大学。

segments.text: Later, the Crystal Palace was moved to South London.
segments.translation: 后来，水晶宫被迁往伦敦南部。

segments.text: It remained one of the most famous buildings in the world until it was burnt down in 1936.
segments.translation: 它一直是世界上最著名的建筑之一，直到1936年被烧毁。
